drivingQuestion: When does a liquid mixed with blood retain the status of blood, and does the nullification that disqualifies sacrificial blood also release one from covering?
outcomeNote: Shmuel's novelty is located in the susceptibility clause and narrowed to self-gathered rainwater; the contradiction about a corpse's liquids is resolved by reading חמורין as a zav, with the decree's rationale supplied.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ תְּנַן הָתָם: דָּם שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵב בְּמַיִם, אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ מַרְאִית דָּם – כָּשֵׁר. נִתְעָרֵב בְּיַיִן – רוֹאִין אוֹתוֹ כְּאִילּוּ הוּא מַיִם. נִתְעָרֵב בְּדַם בְּהֵמָה אוֹ בְּדַם הַחַיָּה – רוֹאִין אוֹתוֹ כְּאִילּוּ הוּא מַיִם. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין דָּם מְבַטֵּל דָּם.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «We learned» in a mishna «there» (Zevaḥim 77b): In the case of «blood» of an offering fit for sacrifice «that was mixed with water, if» the mixture «has the appearance of blood» it is «fit» for sprinkling on the altar, even though the majority of the mixture is water. If the blood «was mixed with» red «wine, one views» the wine «as though it is water.» If that amount of water would leave the mixture with the appearance of blood it is fit for presentation. And likewise, if the blood «was mixed with the blood of» a non-sacred «domesticated animal or the blood of» a non-sacred «undomesticated animal, one considers» the non-sacred blood «as though it is water. Rabbi Yehuda says: Blood does not nullify blood.» Therefore, the priest presents the blood of the mixture on the altar.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁנָּפְלוּ מַיִם לְתוֹךְ דָּם, אֲבָל נָפַל דָּם לְתוֹךְ מַיִם – רִאשׁוֹן רִאשׁוֹן בָּטֵל.
segments.en: The mishna teaches that in a case where water became mixed with the blood of an offering, if the mixture has the appearance of blood it is fit, despite the fact that there is more water than blood. Concerning this «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan says: They taught» this halakha «only» in a case «where» the «water fell into» the «blood. But» in a case where the «blood fell into» the «water,» the «first» drop of blood, and then the next «first» drop of blood, are «nullified» in the water, i.e., each drop is nullified in turn. Consequently, the mixture is unfit for presentation, regardless of whether it has the appearance of blood.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: וּלְעִנְיַן כִּסּוּי אֵינוֹ כֵּן, אֵין דִּחוּי אֵצֶל מִצְוֹת.
segments.en: «Rav Pappa says: But with regard to» the mitzva of «covering» the blood of birds or undomesticated animals that are slaughtered, «it is not so.» In this case, even if the blood fell into water the mitzva of covering applies to it, provided the mixture has the appearance of blood. The blood is not nullified by the water «because there is no» permanent «rejection with regard to mitzvot» other than those that relate to sacrificial rites. Therefore, its nullification was merely temporary, but once there is enough blood in the water it reassumes its status of blood.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כׇּל מַרְאֵה אַדְּמוּמִית – מְכַפְּרִין, וּמַכְשִׁירִין, וְחַיָּיבִין בְּכִסּוּי. מַאי קָמַשְׁמַע לַן? מְכַפְּרִין – תְּנֵינָא, חַיָּיבִין בְּכִסּוּי – תְּנֵינָא!
segments.en: § With regard to mixtures of blood and water, «Rav Yehuda says» that «Shmuel says: All» mixtures of blood and water that maintain «a reddish hue» are considered blood and «effect atonement» by being presented on the altar, «and render» food «susceptible» to contracting ritual impurity, «and are» included in the «obligation of covering» the blood provided that the blood is from the slaughter of an undomesticated animal or bird. The Gemara asks: «What» is Rav Yehuda «teaching us?» If he is teaching us that such mixtures «effect atonement, we» already «learn» this from the mishna in tractate Zevaḥim. And if he is teaching us that such mixtures are included in the «obligation of covering» the blood, «we» already «learn» this in the mishna here.

segments.he: מַכְשִׁירִין אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ. מַכְשִׁירִין נָמֵי, אִי דָּם – אַכְשׁוֹרֵי מַכְשַׁר, אִי מַיָּא – אַכְשׁוֹרֵי מַכְשְׁרִי! לָא צְרִיכָא, שֶׁתִּמְּדוֹ בְּמֵי גְשָׁמִים.
segments.en: Rather, it «was necessary for» Rav Yehuda to teach that such mixtures «render» food «susceptible» to contracting ritual impurity, as this was not taught in a mishna. The Gemara challenges: It is «also» unnecessary to teach that such mixtures «render» food «susceptible» to contracting ritual impurity. «If» the mixture has the status of «blood it renders» food «susceptible,» as does blood, «and if» the mixture has the status of «water it renders» food susceptible, as does water. The Gemara responds: «No,» this statement is «necessary» in a case «where» the blood «was mixed with rainwater,» which does not render food susceptible without the intent or desire of the owner of the food. If the mixture is considered blood it renders food susceptible.

segments.he: מֵי גְשָׁמִים נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּשָׁקֵיל וְרָמֵי, אַחְשְׁבִינְהוּ. לָא צְרִיכָא, שֶׁנִּתְמְדוּ מֵאֲלֵיהֶן.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges: With regard to «rainwater as well, since one took» it «and placed» it into a vessel containing blood, «he has ascribed significance» to the rainwater and it should be capable of rendering food susceptible. The Gemara responds: «No,» this statement is «necessary» in a case «where» the rainwater «was mixed» with the blood «by itself,» i.e., it was not gathered and poured purposefully.

segments.he: רַבִּי אַסִּי מִנְּהַרְבִּיל אוֹמֵר: בִּצְלַלְתָּא דִּדְמָא. רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מִדִּפְתִּי אָמַר: עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת, וְהוּא דְּאִיכָּא כְּזַיִת. בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא: מְטַמְּאִים בְּאֹהֶל, וְהוּא דְּאִיכָּא רְבִיעִית.
segments.en: «Rabbi Asi of Neharbil says:» The statement of Rav Yehuda is referring «to blood plasma,» i.e., if the plasma has a reddish hue due to the blood, it has the status of blood and can render food susceptible to contracting ritual impurity. «Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti said:» Consumption of this plasma is «punishable by karet,» as is the halakha with regard to one who consumes blood (see Leviticus 17:14), «provided that there is» at least one «olive-bulk» of actual blood. «It was taught in a baraita:» Blood plasma that issues from a corpse that has a reddish hue «imparts ritual impurity in a tent, provided that there is» at least «a quarter-»log of actual blood, which is the amount of a corpse’s blood that imparts ritual impurity.

segments.he: תְּנַן הָתָם: כׇּל מַשְׁקֵה הַמֵּת טְהוֹרִין, חוּץ מִדָּמוֹ, וְכׇל מַרְאֵה אַדְּמוּמִית שֶׁבּוֹ מְטַמְּאִין בְּאֹהֶל. וּמַשְׁקֵה הַמֵּת טְהוֹרִין? וּרְמִינְהוּ: מַשְׁקֶה טְבוּל יוֹם, מַשְׁקִין הַיּוֹצְאִין מִמֶּנּוּ כְּמַשְׁקִין שֶׁנּוֹגֵעַ בָּהֶן,
segments.en: «We learned» in a baraita «elsewhere» (Tosefta, Oholot 4:5): «All liquids» that issue «from a corpse,» e.g., teardrops or breastmilk, «are ritually pure, except for its blood. And all» liquids that issue «from» a corpse that contain «a reddish hue» of blood «impart ritual impurity in a tent.» The Gemara asks: «But are liquids» that issue from «a corpse ritually pure? And raise a contradiction» from a mishna (Tevul Yom 2:1): With regard to «liquids» that issue «from one who immersed that day, liquids that issue from him» have the same status «as liquids that he touches.»

segments.he: וְאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ אֵין מְטַמְּאִין, וּשְׁאָר כׇּל הַטְּמֵאִין, בֵּין קַלִּין בֵּין חֲמוּרִין – מַשְׁקִין הַיּוֹצְאִין מֵהֶן כְּמַשְׁקֶה הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּהֶן, וְאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ תְּחִלָּה, חוּץ מִן הַמַּשְׁקֶה שֶׁהוּא אַב הַטּוּמְאָה.
segments.en: «And» both «these and those,» i.e., both liquids that issue from one who immersed himself that day and liquids he touches, «do not impart ritual impurity. And» with regard to «all other» sources of «impurity, whether minor» sources «or major» sources, «liquids that issue from them» have the same status «as liquids that touch them, and» both «these and those have» first-degree ritual impurity, since they touched a primary source of ritual impurity upon exiting the source. This is the halakha «except for a liquid that is» itself «a primary source of» ritual «impurity.»

segments.he: מַאי קַלִּין וּמַאי חֲמוּרִין? מַאי לָאו: קַלִּין – שֶׁרֶץ וְזָב, וַחֲמוּרִין – מֵת? לָא, קַלִּין – שֶׁרֶץ, וַחֲמוּרִין – זָב.
segments.en: The Gemara analyzes the mishna: «What» is the meaning of «minor» sources «and what» is the meaning of «major» sources? «What, is it not» that the term: «Minor» sources, is referring to «a creeping animal or a zav, and» that the term: «Major» sources, is referring to «a corpse?» If so, the mishna teaches that all liquids that issue from a corpse are ritually impure, in contradiction to the baraita. The Gemara responds: «No,» the term: «Minor» sources, is referring to «a creeping animal,» e.g., urine found inside its body, which is not considered ritually impure, «and» the term: «Major» sources, is referring to «a zav,» concerning whom all liquids that issue from him are ritually impure. By contrast, liquids that issue from a corpse are ritually pure with the exception of blood.

segments.he: מַאי שְׁנָא זָב, דִּגְזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן, וּמַאי שְׁנָא מֵת דְּלָא גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן? זָב דְּלָא בְּדִילִי אִינָשֵׁי מִינֵּיהּ – גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן, מֵת דִּבְדִילִי אִינָשֵׁי מִינֵּיהּ – לָא גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «What is different» with regard to «a zav, concerning whom the Sages decreed» that liquids that issue from him are ritually impure, «and what is different» with regard to «a corpse, concerning which the Sages did not decree» that liquids that issue from it are ritually impure? The Gemara responds: In the case of «a zav, since people do not» naturally «separate from him, the Sages decreed» additional restrictions «with regard to him» in order to prevent others from contracting impurity from liquids that issue from a zav that are impure by Torah law. In the case of «a corpse, since people» naturally «separate from it, the Sages did not decree» additional restrictions «with regard to it.»

moves.summary: The parallel Zevahim mishna on blood of an offering mixed with water, wine or other blood is brought.
moves.about: bringing the Zevahim mishna on blood of an offering mixed with water, wine or other blood

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי חייא בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן: לא שנו אלא
moves.summary: Rabbi Yohanan restricts that mishna to where water fell into blood; blood into water is nullified drop by drop.
moves.about: restricting the mishna's fitness ruling to where water fell into blood, since blood falling into water is nullified drop by drop

moves.cueHe: אמר רב פפא: ולענין כסוי אינו כן
moves.summary: Rav Pappa excludes the mitzva of covering, since there is no rejection with regard to mitzvot.
moves.about: confining Rabbi Yohanan's nullification rule to sacrificial blood and excluding the mitzva of covering from it

moves.cueHe: אמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל: כל מראה אדמומית
moves.summary: Shmuel rules that any mixture with a reddish hue atones, renders susceptible, and requires covering.
moves.about: transmitting Shmuel's rule that any mixture with a reddish hue counts as blood for atonement, susceptibility and covering

moves.summary: The gemara objects that atonement and covering are both already taught in mishnayot.
moves.about: that Shmuel's statement teaches nothing new, since atonement and covering are both already taught in mishnayot

moves.summary: The novelty lies in the ruling that such mixtures render food susceptible to impurity.
moves.about: that Shmuel's statement was needed for the ruling that such mixtures render food susceptible to impurity

moves.summary: But blood renders food susceptible and so does water, so that too is superfluous.
moves.about: that the susceptibility ruling too is superfluous, since blood renders food susceptible and so does water

moves.summary: It is needed where the blood was mixed with rainwater, which does not render food susceptible on its own.
moves.about: that the statement is needed where the blood was mixed with rainwater, which does not by itself render food susceptible

moves.summary: Gathering and pouring the rainwater ascribes significance to it, so it should render food susceptible.
moves.about: that rainwater too should render food susceptible, since by taking and pouring it one ascribes significance to it

moves.summary: The case is where the rainwater mixed with the blood by itself.
moves.about: that the case is where the rainwater mixed with the blood by itself, without being gathered and poured

moves.cueHe: רבי אסי מנהרביל אומר: בצללתא דדמא
moves.summary: Rabbi Asi refers Shmuel's rule to blood plasma.
moves.about: referring Shmuel's reddish-hue rule to blood plasma, the clear fluid that separates when blood congeals

moves.cueHe: רבי ירמיה מדפתי אמר: ענוש כרת
moves.summary: Eating such plasma carries karet where an olive-bulk of blood is present.
moves.about: extending the reddish-hue rule to karet liability for consuming such plasma where an olive-bulk of actual blood is present

moves.summary: A baraita adds that such liquids impart tent impurity where a quarter-log of blood is present.
moves.about: extending the reddish-hue rule to a corpse's liquids imparting impurity in a tent, given a quarter-log of blood

moves.summary: A ruling is brought that all liquids of a corpse are pure except its blood, reddish ones imparting tent impurity.
moves.about: bringing the ruling that all liquids of a corpse are pure except its blood, and reddish liquids impart tent impurity

moves.summary: A contradiction is raised from the mishna on liquids issuing from sources of impurity.
moves.about: whether liquids of a corpse are pure, given that liquids issuing from every impure source are said to be impure

moves.summary: The cited mishna continues: liquids from all other impure sources, minor and major alike, have first-degree impurity.
moves.about: bringing the mishna on liquids issuing from one who immersed that day and from other sources of impurity

moves.summary: The gemara asks what the terms minor and major sources mean.
moves.about: what the cited mishna's terms minor sources and major sources of impurity refer to

moves.summary: It floats that major means a corpse, which would make the contradiction stand.
moves.about: floating the reading that major sources includes a corpse, which would make its liquids impure and sustain the contradiction

moves.summary: The floated reading is rejected: minor is a creeping animal and major a zav, so the corpse is not included.
moves.about: rejecting the floated reading and assigning minor to a creeping animal and major to a zav, leaving the corpse out

moves.cueHe: מאי שנא זב דגזרו ביה רבנן
moves.summary: Why did the Sages decree on a zav's liquids and not on a corpse's?
moves.about: why the Sages decreed impurity on liquids issuing from a zav but not on liquids issuing from a corpse

moves.summary: People do not keep away from a zav, so a decree was needed; from a corpse they do keep away.
moves.about: supplying the rationale that people do not keep away from a zav, whereas they do keep away from a corpse
